match.reason: Neither bank point covers how businesses use behavioural insights to influence consumers' purchases; one is about business's role in the economy and the other is about workers' motivation.

draft.title: How businesses use behavioural insights
card: Framing
how an option is presented changes how it feels. Meat labelled 90% lean sounds better than 10% fat, though it is the same.
Anchoring
a first number, such as a high original price, becomes a reference point. A sale price then looks like a bargain.
Loss aversion
people feel a loss more strongly than an equal gain. A free trial that rolls over into a paid plan uses this, as cancelling feels like losing something.
A limited-time offer adds pressure to buy now, before there is time to compare options.
draft.remember: Businesses shape choices through how options are framed, anchored and timed.

a.q: A shop shows a jacket at $200 crossed out, then $120 beside it. Which idea is the shop using?
opts: Anchoring, as $200 becomes the reference point
Framing, as the same price is described two ways
Loss aversion, as the buyer fears losing the jacket
A free trial that rolls over into a paid plan
a.why: The first price of $200 sets a reference point, so $120 seems cheap. This is anchoring. Framing would be describing the same thing in different words.
a.clue: Which number does the buyer see first?

b.q: A streaming service gives a free month that becomes a paid plan unless cancelled. Many users keep paying. Which idea best explains why?
opts: Cancelling feels like a loss of something they already have
The first price shown sets a high reference point
The plan is described in more positive words
A sale ends soon so users must choose quickly
b.why: Once users have the service, giving it up feels like a loss, and loss aversion makes that feel stronger than the saving. The offer is not about a first price or a time limit.
b.clue: Think about how it feels to give up something you already have.

a.best: Anchoring, as $200 becomes the reference point

b.best: Cancelling feels like a loss of something they already have

problems.detail: The clue 'Think about how it feels to give up something you already have' nearly repeats the right option word for word ('a loss of something they already have'), so a student can match the words without knowing loss aversion.
The distractor 'A sale ends soon so users must choose quickly' uses 'must', where the card says a limited-time offer only 'adds pressure' to buy now.
